body:
With `CYTHON_USE_MODULE_STATE=1`, a C function called from `nogil` without an optional argument can crash when its default is an enum member or a Cython-defined numeric const global: reading the stored default needs the GIL. Use these constants directly, sharing the predicate between default-code generation and initialization. Accept `entry.is_const`, including C++ scoped enums, and non-volatile numeric const globals defined by Cython.

External const declarations keep the stored default because they can be read-only views of mutable C storage. External const defaults such as `libc.limits.CHAR_BIT` therefore still need the GIL with module state enabled.

Runtime regressions are in the existing `cyfunction_defaults.pyx` and `cyfunction_defaults_cpp.pyx`. They cover omitted and explicit enum arguments, cimported and qualified members, `cpdef enum`, `DEF`, a Cython-defined const integer, external read-only snapshots, and a builtin default. With #8081's memoryview fix applied, the original enum case crashes on master; C++ scoped enums and the const integer crash without the corresponding parts of this change. The snapshot test checks that changing the underlying C values does not change the defaults.

With module state disabled, the repository runner passes 88 tests for the two `cyfunction_defaults` modules, `cpdef_enums` and `cpp_scoped_enums`. With module state enabled, the defaults modules pass 20 C tests and 26 C++17 tests. These combined runs use #8081's one-line fix for the existing memoryview defaults. The nogil regressions detect these crashes only in module-state builds; with module state disabled, the new C tests also pass without this compiler change.

Without an explicit C++ standard, module-state builds also fail on master with an unrelated `std::atomic` initialization error, so these runs used C++17.

comment_data.body: This isn't currently covered by `cyfunction_defaults` but I'd rather cover it there rather than add a special test.

Superficially (without having tried it) this seems like:
* some `enums` might be attributes rather than names.
* Other things with `is_const` might benefit from the same thing
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -1095,10 +1095,15 @@ def inject_type_from_annotations(self, env):
             self.type_from_annotation = True
         return arg_type
 
+    def _default_is_c_constant(self):
+        default = self.default
+        return default.is_literal or (
+            default.is_name and default.entry.is_const and default.type.is_enum)

comment_data.body:
Moved the regression into `cyfunction_defaults.pyx` and removed the standalone `.srctree` in [9ba3817](https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/8082/commits/9ba3817d1a763b564f711570f61d41b91b9d7128). The C++ scoped-enum case is in the existing `cyfunction_defaults_cpp.pyx`. Coverage through [95f944e](https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/8082/commits/95f944ebddde2774dd7f9600a989b169d983b0ac) also checks numeric const defaults and snapshots of external read-only values.

Both modules pass with module state enabled: 20 C tests and 26 C++17 tests, including the `cpp_locals` variants. These runs use #8081's one-line fix for the existing memoryview defaults. The nogil regressions detect the crashes only in a module-state build; with module state disabled, the new C tests also pass without this compiler change.

Without an explicit C++ standard, module-state builds also fail on master with an unrelated `std::atomic` initialization error, so these runs used C++17.

The predicate now accepts `entry.is_const`, including C++ scoped-enum members, plus non-volatile numeric const globals defined by Cython ([95f944e](https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/8082/commits/95f944ebddde2774dd7f9600a989b169d983b0ac)). The confirmed missing enum case was a C++ scoped enum, which uses `is_cpp_enum` instead of `is_enum`. Cimported `module.ENUM` and qualified C enum members already resolve to `NameNode`; the new nogil tests cover those, `cpdef enum`, `DEF`, and a Cython-defined const integer. The C++ scoped-enum and const-integer cases crash without their respective fixes and pass with module state enabled afterward. A builtin-default identity check also passes.

External const declarations keep the stored default: they can be read-only views of mutable C storage. The new test changes the underlying C values and checks that both const and const-volatile defaults retain their initial values. External const defaults such as `libc.limits.CHAR_BIT` still need the GIL with module state enabled.

commit.message: Use C enum constants directly in default arguments
Share the default C constant predicate
Cover constant defaults in the existing cyfunction tests
Preserve snapshots of volatile default values
Preserve snapshots for external const defaults
